children: Australian shares fell 85 points or 1% to 8,760 in early Tuesday trade, snapping a two-session rise as profit-taking set in after markets hit a near five-week top.
Sentiment was also pressured by renewed churn in global tech stocks and doubts over AI-related spending.

Locally, RBA Assistant Governor Kent noted that rising global neutral rates raise questions about whether policy is restrictive enough despite four hikes this year, tempering confidence in the current stance.
Still, losses were partly offset by stronger-than-expected Q3 GDP and September activity data from China, aided by Golden Week demand.
Tech, logistics, non-energy minerals, and financials drove the downside amid steep losses in heavyweights BHP Group (-2.1%) and Rio Tinto (-1.2%).
The four big banks slumped between 1.5% and 2.7%, while other notable laggards included Northern Star Resources (-2.2%), Evolution Mining (-3.1%), and Qantas Airways (-1.7%).
Traders now await China’s monthly lending rate fix later today.

title: Australian Stocks Retreat from Near 5-Week High
